subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core own generic side-effect claim verification for source-channel final text, or should core stay limited to delivery invariants and support a ClawHub/plugin verifier through hook/API improvements?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans Telegram delivery, agent runtime state, and optional policy enforcement; current code has partial core guardrails, while VISION.md and the closed generic verifier issue favor plugin scope unless core lacks the needed API.

options.title: Keep core narrow
options.body: Core continues to enforce delivery invariants and maintain hook/API support so claim verification can live as a plugin or ClawHub package.

options.title: Add core verification
options.body: Core implements a turn-level side-effect ledger and blocks or annotates unsupported success claims in final text.

options.title: Force tool-only Telegram DMs
options.body: Telegram direct messages default to message_tool_only to reduce visible false-success finals, accepting a compatibility and stranded-reply behavior change.

recommendation.title: Keep core narrow
recommendation.body: Core continues to enforce delivery invariants and maintain hook/API support so claim verification can live as a plugin or ClawHub package.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the same product-boundary choice reflected in the merged warning-only guardrail and the closed generic claim-verification scope decision.
